lead.event: Bank Indonesia cuts reserve requirements and macroprudential liquidity incentives
lead.headline: Bank Indonesia cuts reserve rates to 7% and 5.5%, liquidity incentive to 5%
lead.blurb: Bank Indonesia will lower conventional banks’ reserve requirement from 9% to 8% on 1 November and 7% on 1 December, while Islamic banks’ rate will decline from 7.5% to 6.5% and then 5.5%. It will also reduce the Macroprudential Liquidity Incentive from a maximum of 6% to 5% on 1 December. Governor Destry Damayanti said the staged 2% reserve cut could provide banks with up to Rp190 trillion in additional liquidity. The incentive’s financing-channel maximum will fall from 4% to 3%, while the money-market-deepening maximum remains 2%.
lead.copy_decision: rewritten: regrouped, 4 of its articles moved out

market_structure_policy.event: Indonesia revises 2026 RKAB production quotas for nickel and coal
market_structure_policy.headline: Indonesia revises 2026 nickel ore and coal quotas to about 290 million and 700 million tons
market_structure_policy.blurb: The nickel quota carries a potential ore deficit of 3 million to 87 million tons. Analysts say the changes could affect miners’ production, sales, operating costs and profitability, while coal exports are expected to fall 14% year on year to a maximum of 450 million tons amid domestic market obligations and logistics constraints.

market_structure_policy.event: IDX suspends trading in MSIN and BSWD
market_structure_policy.headline: IDX suspends MSIN and BSWD after BSWD gains 438.33%
market_structure_policy.blurb: The temporary suspensions took effect in the regular and cash markets on 21 October as a cooling-down measure and to protect investors. MNC Digital Entertainment fell 31.21% to 119 in one week, while Bank of India Indonesia, whose shares have high ownership concentration, rose to 8,075 per share; BEI urged market participants to heed company disclosures.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: EMAS plans a private placement of up to 1.47 billion shares
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: EMAS plans private placement of up to 1.47 billion shares
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Merdeka Gold Resources’ controlling shareholder’s stake would fall from 64.83% to 58.94% if all shares are issued, with control unchanged. The placement could raise US$559.05 million, but no investors had expressed interest. Independent shareholders vote on the plan on 26 November.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: TINS secures a DHE-SDA facility from Bank Mandiri
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: TINS signs up to Rp4 trillion DHE-SDA facility with Bank Mandiri
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Timah will use the standby credit line for working capital and liquidity management. The revolving limit is valid for 12 months from signing, while non-revolving drawdowns have tenors of three to 12 months and require blocking DHE-SDA or other funds. Management said the transaction will not affect operations, financial condition or business continuity.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: TBS Energi Utama secures up to S$555 million for waste management expansion
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: TOBA announces up to S$555 million for waste management expansion
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: TBS Energi Utama announced the investment from funds and managed accounts of HPS Investment Partners, part of BlackRock, through staged purchases of newly issued preferred shares in SBTH Asia Holdings, the parent of its waste management platform. The investment requires shareholder approval at an extraordinary meeting, and TBS will retain control.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: CENT secures loan facilities for refinancing
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: CENT secures Rp12.48 trillion in loan facilities for refinancing
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Centratama and subsidiaries signed the agreements on 19 October with 14 creditors, including DBS Bank and MUFG Bank. The facilities will mainly refinance existing loans, cover fees and expenses, and settle hedge-counterparty obligations. Two shareholder loan maturities were extended to 31 December 2031.

deals_control.event: CIMB Group explores privatization and delisting of CIMB Niaga
deals_control.headline: CIMB Group explores BNGA privatization and delisting ahead of 15% float rule
deals_control.blurb: BNGA shares rose 11.29% to Rp1,725 on 21 October. CIMB Niaga says it is still assessing options, with no final decision, while its free float was about 7.5% in September. Reported requirements call for 12.5% by March 2027 and 15% by March 2028.
deals_control.copy_decision: rewritten: 2 new articles with a new fact: BNGA shares rose 11.29% to Rp1,725 on 21 October.

deals_control.event: IPAC shareholders approve privatization and IDX delisting
deals_control.headline: IPAC shareholders approve privatization and IDX delisting with Rp250 tender offer
deals_control.blurb: APAC Investment 2 is offering Rp250 per share for up to 89.31 million public shares, worth about Rp22.33 billion if fully taken up. The approved privatization and delisting remain subject to regulatory processes and approvals, and holders who do not tender may retain shares that no longer trade on the exchange.

deals_control.event: SILO completes the first-stage acquisition of three companies
deals_control.headline: SILO completes first-stage acquisition of three companies for Rp828.67 billion
deals_control.blurb: Siloam and subsidiary Megapratama Karya Bersama completed the purchase of Buton Bangun Cipta, Menara Abadi Megah and Nusa Bahana Niaga. Analysts see potential long-term gains in hospital asset ownership and rental efficiency, but say higher interest and depreciation expenses could weigh on near-term profit.

earnings_guidance.event: PPRE reports a nine-month net loss
earnings_guidance.headline: PPRE reports a Rp161.61 billion nine-month net loss
earnings_guidance.blurb: PP Presisi swung from a Rp104.97 billion profit in January-September 2025 as revenue rose 19.86% to Rp3.32 trillion. Cost of revenue climbed 34.25% to Rp2.94 trillion, while gross profit fell 33.03% to Rp387.06 billion.

earnings_guidance.headline: PGEO targets 1.8 GW of installed capacity by 2034
earnings_guidance.blurb: Pertamina Geothermal Energy aims to reach 1 GW by 2028, up from 727 MW currently, with estimated investment of US$5.36 billion to US$6.43 billion. It plans to use internal capital, remaining IPO proceeds and green financing, alongside a joint venture with PLN; Lumut Balai Unit 3 is slated to start commercial operations in 2029.

earnings_guidance.event: Samuel Sekuritas assigns TINS a Buy rating
earnings_guidance.headline: Samuel Sekuritas gives TINS a Buy rating with a Rp5,000 target price
earnings_guidance.blurb: Managing Director Harry Su cited tight global tin supply and positive prospects, with a 5,720-ton market deficit in 1H26. Timah posted Rp2.71 trillion in first-half net profit, above its initial full-year target of Rp1.61 trillion. Risks include a tin price correction, weaker electronics demand, and the need to raise production and control costs.

earnings_guidance.event: Phapros sets 2026 sales and profit growth targets
earnings_guidance.headline: PEHA targets over 20% sales growth and double-digit profit growth in 2026
earnings_guidance.blurb: At a public expose, Phapros allocated Rp68.7 billion for capital expenditure. Analyst Surya Rianto says reaching the targets requires Rp646.21 billion in additional revenue beyond first-half sales of Rp482.85 billion and a net profit margin of around 3%, which would lift net profit 23% to Rp33.87 billion.

macro_flows.event: Bank Indonesia holds the BI Rate at 5.75%
macro_flows.headline: Bank Indonesia holds BI Rate at 5.75%
macro_flows.blurb: At its 20–21 October meeting, it raised the Deposit Facility rate to 5% and kept the Lending Facility rate at 6.50%. The BI Rate has now been unchanged for five consecutive meetings after a 25-basis-point increase in June.

macro_flows.event: MSCI's Indonesia reclassification consultation and market responses
macro_flows.headline: MSCI opens Indonesia reclassification consultation, decision due by 30 June 2027
macro_flows.blurb: The IHSG fell 11.57% on 16 October to 5,185. The proposal would shift Indonesia from Emerging Market to Standalone Market, but its status remains unchanged during the consultation as MSCI freezes certain index changes for Indonesian stocks. Feedback is open through 30 April 2027, with a final decision due no later than 30 June 2027.
macro_flows.copy_decision: rewritten: regrouped, 2 of its articles moved out

macro_flows.event: Chinese nickel producers consider coordinated Indonesian output cuts
macro_flows.headline: Chinese nickel producers consider roughly 30% cuts at Indonesian HPAL facilities
macro_flows.blurb: The proposal would apply to each company’s Indonesian HPAL facilities, which produce mixed hydroxide precipitate for battery-grade nickel. Executives from Tsingshan Holding Group, GEM, Lygend Resources & Technology and Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt are scheduled to meet to finalize the plan, but no agreement is guaranteed.
macro_flows.copy_decision: rewritten: moved from flash to story

macro_flows.event: Indonesia's investment risk premium rises toward 100 basis points
macro_flows.headline: Indonesia's investment risk premium rises toward 100 basis points
macro_flows.blurb: Five-year CDS briefly approached 100 before easing to around 99 on 21 October, ahead of BI's rate announcement. A proposed MSCI downgrade and weaker sukuk demand added pressure, with auction bids falling 30% to Rp22.76 trillion from Rp32.61 trillion at the previous auction.
